title: Evaluation techniques for storage hierarchies
authors: Mattson, R.L. and Gecsei, J. and Slutz, D. R. and Traiger, I. L.

title: Performance evaluation and prediction of storage hierarchies
abstract: This paper proposes a modelling methodology combining simulation and analysis for computer performance evaluation and prediction. The methodology is based on a special workload model that is suitable for the generation and description of dynamic program behaviour. A description of this workload model is given in section 2. The applicability of this concept with respect to the design of new storage systems, as well as the improvement or comparison of existing systems, will be described by investigation of the efficiency of small cache memories in section 3.

title: L19725 Utilizing Microseismic Techniques for the Evaluation of Underground Gas Storage Reservoir Stability
abstract:
In light of the recent energy crisis, the desirability of storing fuels close to primary distribution areas has assumed an even greater importance than in the past. The natural gas industry is faced with the problem of locating and developing sufficient underground storage reservoir capacity in high demand areas to meet peak seasonal requirements.

Since it is economically desirable to store gas at the maximum possible pressure, studies to estimate optimum operating pressures for underground gas storage reservoirs and to evaluate their stability under such operating conditions.
